Subject: Charge mismatch on AWS Marketplace invoice 1234567890

Hi Markus,

We're seeing a discrepancy between the AWS Marketplace invoice attached (aws-invoice-1234567890.pdf) and the metering export we pulled for March. The invoice total includes a VAT line that doesn't match the itemized usage rows in our export — the VAT looks like it was applied to reseller fees rather than end-customer consumption in a few EU countries.

We run our own metering and the attached CSV (gigastore-metering-export-20260321.csv) shows three marketplace transactions on 2026-02-28 where the tax amount is missing from the itemized line. As a result, our accounting team is pausing payment pending reconciliation. Can you confirm how Redwood remits VAT for marketplace sales (if Redwood is the listed seller) vs how AWS presents tax on the invoice? Also if Redwood can provide a breakdown by invoice line with tax codes, that would help us close our books.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — we need to make a decision on the payment hold by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Erin Cole
Finance Ops
Gigastore Inc.

Markus/All,

Quick update from billing ops after a first-pass compare (attached diff and line-item map). High-level:
- AWS invoice #1234567890 includes VAT on three line items billed to EU customers (DE, FR, NL). Our metering export shows the usage lines but the tax_code field is empty for those rows in our export (looks like a mapping issue between our reseller metadata and the marketplace usage feed).
- AWS appears to be calculating VAT on the gross reseller charge for those customers, which is why the invoice total is higher than our net usage-based figure.
- We need AWS to provide the original tax breakdown (taxable base, tax rate, country code) — that will let us determine whether Redwood or AWS is responsible for remitting VAT under the contract for those customers.

Next steps I’m executing now:
1) Submitting a formal ticket with AWS billing with request id AWS-CASE-75492 and asking for per-line tax breakout and any reseller tax handling notes.
2) Running an internal script to re-export the metering with the full reseller metadata and tax_code mapping — I’ll attach the result when ready.
3) If AWS confirms they collected VAT incorrectly, we’ll request a credit and issue a corrected invoice to Gigastore.

ETA: I should have the re-export and AWS case number back by EOD Monday.

- Prioym
Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) AWS: please provide the per-invoice, per-line tax breakdown for invoice 1234567890 (taxable base, tax rate, country code) and confirm whether AWS withheld/collected VAT at invoice generation time (AWS case ref: AWS-CASE-75492).
2) Redwood (billing ops): will deliver a matched reconciliation file that maps Redwood usage lines to AWS invoice lines, including our reseller metadata and proposed tax_code mapping (redwood-metering-export-20260321.csv + billing-diff-1234567890.csv).
3) If AWS confirms over-collection or misapplied VAT, AWS/Redwood will coordinate a credit and corrected invoice; Redwood will notify Gigastore and provide a JIR/credit reference for their accounting team.

Timeline: request to AWS sent now; expect AWS response 3 business days. Redwood will aim to produce the matched reconciliation within 48 hours of AWS tax breakdown. Credit (if required) to appear on next AWS billing cycle or via an off-cycle credit depending on AWS policy.
